criteria.criterion: Every question in quiz.json tests a point about the target of the change that the case brief states
criteria.reason: Every question tests a point of the brief's target: the split-delta leak and why per-delta redaction missed it (q1), stopping fragments before listeners (q2), the longest-secret-minus-one hold and its safety invariant (q3, q4), that hold's lag and release (q5), flush at assistant-message end (q6), never cutting a surrogate pair (q7), and their combination (q8).

criteria.criterion: Every question sits at an altitude that the case brief allows, as the brief describes that altitude
criteria.reason: All questions sit at mechanism altitude: they test inputs (deltas), state (the held buffer), invariants (no emitted text can join into a secret, no split surrogates), and failure modes (fragment leaks), without dipping into function names or signatures.

criteria.criterion: No question asks about an incidental part of the change that the case brief lists
criteria.reason: No question asks about test helper names or the variable names in pi.ts; the merged-secret-map mention in q3's key points states the invariant that the window is sized from the same map the redactor matches, not the incidental hoist.

criteria.criterion: Every wrong option of a single or multi question is a plausible misreading of the change, not filler
criteria.reason: Wrong options are genuine misreadings: redaction only at reply end, streams never redacted, listener-side sliding windows, an engine recall at message end, lag proportional to reply length, flush at the next user prompt, and a step-back that breaks safety — each something a half-understanding would produce.

criteria.criterion: Each question's key_points state what a correct answer must cover, at the same altitude as the question
criteria.reason: Each question carries key_points that state what a correct answer must cover (the whole-only redaction rule, the dispatch irreversibility, the prefix-within-tail argument, the flush guarantee, the surrogate step-back), and each stays at its question's mechanism level.

criteria.criterion: The questions go outside in: the first ones cover what the change is for and its main boundary, narrower mechanisms and details come later, and no question is more central to the change than one asked before it, except the last
criteria.reason: The order runs outside in: purpose of the change (q1), its main boundary before listeners (q2), the core hold invariant (q3) and its what-if (q4), then narrower facets — cost (q5), flush lifecycle (q6), surrogate detail (q7) — with the integrative case last; relevance drops from core to important and never rises.

criteria.criterion: When quiz.json has two or more questions, the last one applies several points of the change to one new case the change does not spell out
criteria.reason: q8 applies several points of the change — the hold across text blocks, joined redaction of held text plus delta, the surrogate cut-back, and the flush on abort — to one concrete walkthrough scenario the change itself does not spell out.

criteria.criterion: Every question can be answered by a person who understands what the change does and why, with the code closed: no question depends on recalling a function name, a file name, a flag, an exit code, or an exact value, unless that name or value is itself the point the author must own
criteria.reason: Every question is answerable from understanding the mechanism with the code closed; the only names or values used (longest - 1, the high surrogate, the message-end flush) are themselves the point the author must own, and behavior is described inline in the prompts.

criteria.criterion: Every prompt, option, and key point is plain English: short sentences, common words, one idea each, with no jargon the question does not need and no filler or marketing words
criteria.reason: Prompts, options, and key points are plain English: mostly short single-point sentences built from common words, jargon limited to what the mechanism needs (delta, surrogate, flush), and no filler or marketing language.
